title: Why We Need Speech to Evaluate Speech Translation
abstract: arXiv:2605.28227v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Speech translation models are increasingly capable of preserving speech-specific information (e.g., speaker gender, prosody, and emphasis), yet evaluation metrics remain blind to such phenomena. We meta-evaluate both text- and speech-based quality estimation metrics on two contrastive datasets targeting gender agreement and prosody, and find that both fall short, even when given direct access to the speech signal. We then train SpeechCOMET, a family of quality estimation models with speech encoders, and evaluate a state-of-the-art SpeechLLM as a judge. Both match or exceed text-based COMET on standard quality estimation, but neither consistently assesses speech-specific phenomena. We identify three causes: (1) speech-specific features are not reliably preserved in current encoders, (2) models tend to ignore the speech source signal, and (3) quality estimation training data contains too few relevant examples. translated_title: 为什么我们需要语音来评估语音翻译
translated_abstract: 语音翻译模型在保留语音特有信息（如说话人性别、韵律和重音）方面的能力日益增强，然而现有的评估指标却无法察觉这些现象。我们在两个针对性别一致性和韵律的对比数据集上，对基于文本和基于语音的质量估计指标进行了元评估，发现两者均表现不佳，即使它们能够直接获取语音信号。随后，我们训练了SpeechCOMET——一系列带有语音编码器的质量估计模型，并评估了最先进的SpeechLLM作为评判者。两者在标准质量估计任务上达到或超过了基于文本的COMET，但都不能持续有效地评估语音特有现象。我们识别出三个原因：（1）当前的编码器无法可靠地保留语音特有特征；（2）模型倾向于忽略语音源信号；（3）质量估计训练数据中相关样本过少。我们发布了所有模型及……
tldr: 该论文通过元评估揭示现有文本和语音评估指标均无法有效评估语音翻译中的语音特有现象，并训练出SpeechCOMET模型，识别出编码器特征保留不足、模型忽略语音源信号、训练数据匮乏这三大原因。
en_tdlr: This paper meta-evaluates text- and speech-based quality estimation metrics, trains SpeechCOMET with speech encoders, and identifies three causes why current metrics fail to assess speech-specific phenomena, arguing that speech itself is necessary to evaluate speech translation.
